text:
One day, a group of friendly kids went to the park together. They were all very excited. One of the kids started to whistle, and it was so beautiful that everyone else had to join in! The group of kids whistled together for a long time.
Suddenly, the kids heard a faint noise, coming from the trees. They stopped their whistling and wondered what the sound was, when they noticed a friendly squirrel standing on a branch.
The squirrel looked at all of the kids and whistled to them. The kids jumped with excitement, and the squirrel hopped down from the tree. The kids said, "Hi squirrel! What's your name?"
The squirrel smiled and whistled at them. He pointed to his chest, and the kids could just make out the word 'Nutty' in his deep, gentle whistle. The kids laughed, excited to have a new friend called Nutty.
They all spent the afternoon playing together in the park, and Nutty the squirrel got to join the group. The kids waved goodbye to Nutty as he ran up the tree, and they went home with big smiles, happy to have made a new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a cheerful bird named Bob. Bob loved to fly high in the sky. One sunny day, Bob saw a cord hanging from a tree. He was curious and wanted to see what it was.
Bob flew down and said to his friend, the squirrel, "What is this cord for?" The squirrel replied, "It's for the swing. We can play on it and have fun!" Bob was excited and wanted to try it.
Bob and the squirrel took turns swinging on the cord. They laughed and played all day. They were very happy to have found the cord and made a fun game out of it. And from that day on, the cheerful bird and his friend enjoyed playing on the swing together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim and a little girl named Lily. They were best friends. They liked to play together and share their toys. One day, they wanted to make a big picture for their mommies. They needed scissors to cut the paper.
Tim had some scissors, but Lily did not. Tim said, "Lily, we can share my scissors. It is easy to use them." Lily was happy that Tim wanted to share. They took turns using the scissors to cut the paper. They were very careful because scissors can be sharp.
When they finished cutting the paper, they made a beautiful picture. They showed their mommies and said, "Look, we made this together! We shared the scissors and it was easy." Their mommies were very proud of them for sharing and working together.

Once upon a time, there was a brave cow named Bessie. Bessie loved to skip and play in the big green field. She had many friends who liked to play with her. They would skip, run, and jump all day long.
One day, Bessie saw a big truck come to the farm. The truck was taking the cows to a new place. Bessie was excited to go on a trip. She thought it would be fun to see new things and make new friends. So, she got in the truck with the other cows.
When the truck stopped, Bessie found out that the new place was not fun at all. The cows were put in a small pen and they could not skip or play. Bessie missed her big green field and her friends. She was very sad and wished she could go back home. The unexpected thing was that the new place was not a happy place for cows like Bessie. The brave cow's adventure did not have a happy ending.

One day, a boy named Tim saw a pale caterpillar. He wanted to introduce the caterpillar to his friend, Jane. Tim took the caterpillar to Jane's house. He knocked on the door.
"Jane, look what I found!" Tim said. "I want to introduce you to my new friend, Mr. Caterpillar!"
Jane looked at the pale caterpillar and smiled. "Hi, Mr. Caterpillar!" she said. They both played with the caterpillar in the garden.
After a while, they said goodbye to Mr. Caterpillar. Tim and Jane were happy they got to meet and play with their new friend.

Once upon a time, there was a little frog named Tim. Tim loved to jump all day long. One day, while Tim was jumping, he saw a big rock on the ground. He thought it would be fun to jump on the rock.
Tim jumped on the rock, but it felt very uncomfortable. "Ouch!" he said. Just then, the rock started to move! "I'm not a rock, I'm a turtle!" said the turtle. Tim was so surprised!
From that day on, Tim and the turtle became best friends. They played and jumped together, and Tim learned to be more careful about what he jumped on. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a sad little girl. The girl had an idea to make herself feel better. She decided to perform a special job! She took a nail from her dad's toolbox and went outside. She found a big piece of wood in the garden. With one big hammer swing, the nail went into the wood. With every swing, the little girl felt better and better. She hammered the nail in and out of the wood and soon she had made a beautiful pattern.
When she was finished, she felt much happier. She had performed a special job and her sadness had gone away! The little girl was so proud of her work that she showed it to her parents. They were so proud of her too and gave her a big hug. The little girl was so happy she had a smile on her face all day.

One day, a big cat and a little mouse were playing outside. The big cat was very selfish and did not like to share his toys. The little mouse wanted to play with the big cat's toys, but the big cat said, "No! These are my toys!"
Suddenly, there was an emergency! A big storm came and knocked down a tree. The big cat and little mouse were scared. They needed to find a safe place to hide. The big cat thought of his toy house, but it was too small for both of them.
The little mouse had an idea. He said, "I have a big toy house that we can both hide in!" The big cat was surprised. The little mouse was not selfish like the big cat. They both went to the little mouse's big toy house and hid from the storm. The big cat learned to share and not be selfish. From that day on, they displayed their toys together and played happily.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy had a small garden where she liked to grow flowers. One day, she found a wild seed and planted it in her garden.
As the days went by, Amy watered the seed and watched it grow. It grew taller and taller, and soon, it was a big plant. One day, a pretty flag appeared on the plant. The flag was red, blue, and yellow.
Amy was so happy to see the flag. She ran to show her mom and dad. They were proud of her for helping the wild seed grow. They all danced and laughed around the flag, and it was a fun day for everyone.

Lily was a little girl and she loved going for walks. Every day, Lily went for a walk, but she was always frightened. She was a little scared of the animals and people she saw along the way.
One day, her mum suggested that they go on a longer journey. Lily was worried but her mum promised her that, if she was brave and persevered, things would improve.
So, Lily set off on the longer walk with her mum and every day, as they went further and further, Lily got less scared. She looked forward to their new adventures and, soon enough, no longer felt frightened by the animals and people she saw along the way.
At the end of their long journey, Lily could not believe how she'd improved. She was so proud and excited to be able to walk without being scared. It was all because of her determination and her mum's understanding and support.

Anna was very excited. Today was her birthday and she hoped to get a gift from her mom and dad. She woke up early and ran to the living room. She noticed a big box with a bow on the table. She smiled and clapped her hands.
She wanted to open the box right away, but her mom and dad were still sleeping. She tried to be quiet, but she was too curious. She tiptoed to the box and touched the bow. She wondered what was inside. Maybe a doll, or a book, or a puzzle.
She heard a noise from the box. It sounded like a squeak. She gasped and jumped back. What was that? She leaned closer and listened. She heard another squeak, and then a scratch. She felt scared and excited at the same time.
She decided to open the box. She pulled the bow and lifted the lid. She saw a small, furry animal with big ears and a long tail. It was a bunny! It looked at her with bright eyes and twitched its nose. It was the best gift ever!
She picked up the bunny and hugged it. It was soft and warm. It licked her cheek and made her giggle. She named it Fluffy and carried it to her mom and dad's room. She knocked on the door and said, "Look, look, I got a gift! It's a bunny! It's Fluffy!"
Her mom and dad woke up and smiled. They were happy to see her happy. They hugged her and Fluffy and wished her a happy birthday. They said they were proud of her for being so persistent and brave. They said they loved her very much. Anna was very happy. She thanked them and kissed them. She said she loved them and Fluffy too. She said it was the best birthday ever.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to count. He would count everything he saw. One day, Tim went outside to play. He saw a big white cloud in the sky. He started to count the clouds.
As Tim was counting, he saw a gray bird. The gray bird was flying near the white cloud. The gray bird was very fast. Tim tried to count how many times the gray bird flew around the white cloud. But the gray bird was too fast for Tim to count.
Then, something unexpected happened. The gray bird stopped flying and landed next to Tim. The gray bird started to count with Tim! They counted the white clouds together. Tim was very happy. He made a new friend who loved to count just like him. And they counted together every day.

Once upon a time, in a dark, dark town, there was a law. The law said that everyone must match their socks. All the people in the town had to follow this law. They only wore socks that matched. They were very careful to make sure their socks matched every day.
One day, a little girl named Sally went to her sock drawer. She looked for socks that matched. But, oh no! She could not find a match for her favorite pink sock. Sally was very sad. She did not want to break the law, but she also wanted to wear her favorite sock.
Sally put on her favorite pink sock and a white sock. She went outside to play. She was scared that someone would see her socks did not match. But then, something unexpected happened. All the other kids in the town were wearing socks that did not match too! They were all tired of the law and wanted to wear their favorite socks, even if they did not match. So, from that day on, everyone in the town wore socks that did not match, and they were all very happy.

Once upon a time there was a nice arrow. It sat in the middle of a big field all by itself. Then one day, a boy with a bow and arrow came by. He took aim and closed his eyes. Suddenly, the arrow flew across the sky! The arrow flew straight and true and landed right in the middle of the field. The boy was so happy and grateful that he yelled a loud "Yippee!" He ran to pick up the arrow and went on his way.
The arrow was so happy to have been taken away and used that it promised it would never open its eyes again. The arrow stayed closed and thanked the boy for choosing it. The arrow was grateful for the adventure it had been on!

Lily liked to help her mom with the laundry. She put the dirty clothes in the big basket and carried it to the washing machine. She pushed the buttons and watched the water fill up. She liked the bubbles and the noise.
"Can I help you hang the clothes?" she asked her mom.
"Of course, sweetie. You are such a good helper," her mom said. She gave Lily some clothespins and showed her how to clip the clothes on the line. Lily tried to reach the high ones, but she was too small.
"I wish I could grow taller," she said.
"You will, honey. You are growing every day. You just need some time and some food and some sleep," her mom said. She lifted Lily up and helped her hang a shirt.
Lily smiled. She liked being up high. She saw the sun and the birds and the flowers. She felt the wind on her face.
"Look, mom. I'm big now," she said.
Her mom hugged her and kissed her cheek.
"Yes, you are. And I'm so proud of you," she said.

Once upon a time, there was a bear who was the best dancer in the forest. Everywhere he went, he would dance and make his friends happy. But one day, he came upon an enormous log blocking the path. He wanted to dance, but he couldn't find a way to get around the log.
He asked the forest animals for help, but none of them could help him. He became sad and frustrated. Then one of them said, “Bear, if you can’t go around the log, you can go over it!”
The bear started to climb on top of the log and soon he was dancing again. All the animals watched him, amazed by his courage.
The moral of the story is that if you can’t go around the problem, you should try to go over it!

One day, a cute frog was playing near a pond. The frog saw a big leaf. The frog wanted to make a boat with the leaf. So, the frog started to fold the leaf to make the boat.
As the frog was folding the leaf, a little bug came by. The bug said, "Hi frog, what are you doing?" The frog said, "I am making a boat with this leaf." The bug asked, "Can I help you?" The frog said, "Yes, you can help me fold the leaf."
The frog and the bug worked together to fold the leaf. But, as they were folding the leaf, something unexpected happened. The leaf turned into a real boat! The frog and the bug were very surprised. They got into the boat and had a fun day on the pond.

One day, a boy named Tim saw a little toy boat. It was a fragile yacht. Tim liked the boat a lot. He wanted to play with it in the water.
Tim took the boat to the pond. He urged the boat to go fast. The boat went fast in the water. Tim was happy to see the boat go fast.
But the boat was fragile. It broke into pieces. Tim was sad. He took the pieces home. His mom helped him fix the boat. Now, Tim can play with the boat again.

Once upon a time, there was a little jet. The jet had a rough outside. One day, the jet saw a big cloud. The cloud was sad.
The jet flew to the cloud and asked, "Why are you sad?" The cloud said, "I am sad because I am rough too, and no one likes to be near me."
The jet told the cloud, "I am rough too, but we can still be friends." They played together and had fun. Then, a big sun appeared in the sky. The sun saw the jet and the cloud playing together.
The sun said, "You two are good friends even though you are rough. You teach us that we can be friends with anyone, no matter how they look." The jet and the cloud smiled and continued to play, happy to be friends with each other.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She loved to travel with her family. One day, they went to a big forest. In the forest, there were many tall trees. Lucy saw a big pine tree and was glad.
Lucy said to her mom, "Look, mom! A big pine tree!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, it is very big and pretty." They walked and played near the pine tree. Lucy found a pine cone and showed it to her dad. Her dad said, "That's a nice pine cone, Lucy!"
After playing, Lucy and her family were tired. They sat under the big pine tree to rest. They were very glad to have traveled to the forest and found the big pine tree. They had a lot of fun and went home happy.

Mia and her mum were walking. Mia was very excited, as she held a medal in her hand. “Mum, where are we going?” Inquired Mia. “We are going to get our surprise” Her mum replied with a smile.
Suddenly, they heard a loud ringing noise. Mia jumped in surprise and looked around. Then, she saw it - the big red bell on top of the building. Mia felt very nervous, but also excited.
Mia and her mum walked up the steps. They followed the pathway to the big red bell. Mia was shaking as she and her mum slowly made their way to the top. The ringing sound was so loud and Mia felt very nervous. But then, her mum said “it’s time to pull the bell, Mia”.
Mia took a deep breath and closed her eyes. Then, she reached out and pulled the big red bell. All of a sudden, the bell began to ring loudly. Mia was so relieved as she opened her eyes and saw the beautiful surprise - a shiny golden medal.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lena who loved to jump rope. Every day, she'd tie the rope between two trees in her backyard and begin to jump.
One day, Lena's dad went outside and asked her, "Lena, why don't you take a break and check out the file I put on your desk?"
But Lena was in the middle of a jump, so with a big smile, she said, "No thanks, I'm having too much fun."
Lena's dad scratched his head and said, "Lena, remember it's important to mix up all the things in your life. Too much of anything can make you dizzy."
Lena understood. She thought about all the things she liked to do, like drawing, reading and playing tag. She smiled at her dad and said, "Okay, I'll take a break and go look at the file."
The moral of the story is that it's important to mix up your activities and not do too much of one thing. Too much of anything can make you dizzy.

John was feeling gloomy. He was playing in his room when his mom called him. She asked, "John, can you come to the kitchen please?".
John went to the kitchen. His mom had a big bowl, and she asked him to mix in it. John liked mixing things, so he did it eagerly. He felt proud when his mom said to him, "You did a great job. Now it's time to wrap it."
John watched how his mom took the wrap and spread it over the bowl. When it was done, his mom told him, "It's all finished, John. Let's go show it to dad".
Dad liked the bowl that John and mom had mixed and wrapped. He smiled and said, "A job well done". John smiled happily; he had helped his mom make something special.

Lily and Tom were twins who liked to play outside. One day, they saw a big red ball in their uncle's yard. They wanted to play with it, but their uncle was not home. They thought he would not mind if they borrowed it for a little while.
They took the ball and ran to the park. They had fun kicking it, throwing it, and rolling it. They did not see the sign that said "Keep off the grass". They did not hear the angry voice of the gardener who was working there.
"Hey, you kids! Get off my lawn! And give me that ball! It belongs to the mayor!" the gardener shouted. He ran after them with a rake.
Lily and Tom were scared. They dropped the ball and ran away. They hoped the gardener would not catch them. They hoped their uncle would not find out.
But he did. When they got home, their uncle was waiting for them. He looked very mad. He had the ball in his hand. He had a big hole in it.
"Where did you get this ball? Do you know how much trouble you are in? This ball was a gift from the mayor. He was going to give it to the children's hospital. Now it is ruined. And the gardener told me what you did. You broke his rules and his flowers. You are very naughty and rude!" their uncle scolded them.
Lily and Tom felt very bad. They wished they had not taken the ball. They wished they had listened to the sign. They wished they had been nice to the gardener. They said they were sorry, but their uncle was still angry. He said they had to pay for the ball and the flowers. He said they had to go to bed without dinner. He said they had to write a letter of apology to the mayor and the gardener.
Lily and Tom regretted what they did. They learned their lesson. They never took things that were not theirs again. They never played on the grass again. They never made their uncle mad again.

Once upon a time, there was a restless little girl named Lily. She loved to play with her toys all day long. One day, she found a big box in her room. She did not know what was inside, but she wanted to find out.
Lily tried to push the big box, but it was too heavy for her. She thought and thought about how to move the box. Then, she had an idea! She ran to the kitchen and found a scale. She put the scale next to the box and tried to push the box onto the scale. It took a lot of work, but she did it!
When the box was on the scale, Lily saw that the numbers went up. She knew that the box was very heavy. She ran to her mom and told her about the box. Her mom smiled and said, "I put that box there for you. It's a surprise!" Lily's mom helped her open the box, and inside was a brand new toy! Lily was so happy and played with her new toy all day long.

Once upon a time, there were two intelligent ducks who lived in a pond. They had a lot of fun, quacking and swimming together.
One day, they found that a big wreck had shown up in their pond. The wreck was made of wood and was blocking the water.
The two ducks started quacking away, trying to figure out what to do.
"We need to fix this wreck," one duck said.
"Let's work together to move it," said the other.
So, the ducks worked together and moved the wreck away from the pond. From that day on, they had even more fun swimming and quacking together.
The moral of the story is that two heads are better than one. Working together we can accomplish things that no one can do on their own.

Once upon a time, in a big green jungle, there lived a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play outside. His favorite thing to do was swing on the vines. One day, while swinging, he saw a big tiger. The tiger was far away, but Tim knew he would see the tiger again soon.
The big tiger liked to play too. He saw Tim swinging and wanted to join him. But he was too shy to ask. So, the big tiger watched Tim from behind the trees. Tim felt like someone was watching him, but he didn't know it was the big tiger.
A few days later, Tim was swinging again. This time, the big tiger came out from behind the trees. Tim was scared at first, but the big tiger smiled. They both started to swing together. Tim and the big tiger became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, in a quiet little town, there lived a lawyer named Tom. He was a kind and friendly man. Every day, he went to work to help people. Tom loved his job very much.
One sunny day, Tom was going to work when he saw a big turtle in the road. The turtle was very slow and was delaying Tom. He decided to help the turtle cross the road. Tom picked up the turtle and put it on the other side.
But then, something unexpected happened! The turtle started to talk! "Thank you, Tom," said the turtle. "I am a magic turtle, and I will give you one wish for helping me." Tom was very surprised. He thought for a moment and wished for a day off from work to spend with his family. The turtle granted his wish, and Tom had a great day with his family.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to play outside with his dog, Spot. One day, they went to the park to play.
At the park, Tim found a big rock. He thought it was special because it was hidden under a bush. Tim said to Spot, "Look, I found a rock! Let's bury it and come back later to find it." Spot barked happily.
Tim dug a hole with his hands and put the rock in it. He covered it with dirt and put a stick on top. "Now we can find it later," he said. Spot barked again. They played more and went home. They had a fun day at the park with their hidden rock.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his blocks. He would stack them high, making tall towers. One day, Tim wanted to make the tallest stack ever.
Tim started to stack the blocks very high. He was very careful because the blocks were fragile. He did not want them to break. As he was stacking, his friend Sue came over to play. Sue saw the tall stack and was amazed.
Sue asked Tim if she could help him stack the blocks. Tim said yes, and they both worked together. They made the tallest stack ever. Tim and Sue were so happy and proud of their big stack. They played with the blocks all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lily. She loved to watch the birds outside her window. One day, she saw an unusual bird with a very long foot.
Lily wanted to see the bird up close. So, she went outside and followed the bird. The bird hopped and flew from tree to tree. Lily watched the bird's long foot as it moved.
Finally, the bird stopped and looked at Lily. She smiled and waved at the bird. The bird waved its long foot back at her. They became friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Amy. Amy loved the color yellow. She had a yellow dress, a yellow hat, and even a yellow door on her house.
One day, Amy was playing outside when she saw a big yellow ball. She wanted to gain the ball, so she ran to it. But when she got close, something unexpected happened. The ball started to move away from her.
Amy chased the ball all the way to her yellow door. When she opened the door, she saw a big surprise. Inside her house was a big, yellow dog! The dog had been moving the ball with its nose. Amy was so happy to have a new friend. She named the dog Sunny, and they played together every day.

One day, a boy named Tim and his dog, Max, went to the park. They saw a man playing some interesting music. The man said, "I play jazz!" Tim and Max liked the jazz music a lot.
Tim and Max walked and found a big hole. Tim said, "Let's bury something!" They put a toy in the hole and covered it with dirt. They were happy to bury the toy.
Later, they heard the jazz man yell, "Oh no! My special jazz hat is gone!" Tim and Max went back to the hole. They dug up the toy and found the jazz hat under it! The jazz man was so happy. They all laughed and danced to the jazz music.

Once upon a time there was a girl who wanted to make something yummy. She had a pear in her hand and decided to prepare it.
She started by washing it carefully, then she cut it into small pieces.
Finally, she added a bit of sugar on top and looked at the result. It looked delicious!
The girl was happy with her work, but she was missing something. She thought for a moment. Suddenly, she remembered somebody who had been very helpful to her before.
She asked her helper to join her so that they could enjoy the pear together.
The helper was happy to help, of course. The two of them sat down and started eating the tasty pear.
They were so happy with the snack they had prepared together.

Once upon a time, there was a pretty computer. It had a big, bright screen and many fun games. The computer lived in a room where all the kids would come and play.
One day, a little boy named Tim came to play with the computer. He said, "Hello, pretty computer! Let's play a game together!" The computer liked Tim and they played a fun game.
Later, Tim wanted to show the computer to his friends. He said, "Come on, friends! Let's gather and see my pretty computer!" All the kids came and they all played games together. They had a very fun day.

One day, a boy named Tom went to the park. He saw his friend, Sam. Sam was riding a bike with pedals. Tom wanted to ride a bike too, but he did not know how to tie his shoes. His shoes kept coming off when he tried to pedal. Sam said, "I can help you tie your shoes."
Sam showed Tom how to tie his shoes. Tom tried and tried, but he could not do it. Then, a big, healthy dog came running over. The dog picked up Tom's shoe in its mouth. The dog was trying to help Tom tie his shoe!
Tom laughed and said, "Thank you, dog!" The dog helped Tom tie his shoes. Now, Tom could ride a bike with Sam. They had lots of fun at the park. The big, healthy dog went home with Tom and became his new best friend.

Lily liked to play with her lizard, Leo. Leo was green and had a long tail. He liked to eat bugs and run on the rocks. Lily and Leo were friends.
One day, Lily wanted to teach Leo a new trick. She put a bug on a stick and held it in front of Leo. She said, "Leo, jump and catch the bug!" Leo looked at the bug and jumped. He missed the bug and fell on the ground. Lily said, "Try again, Leo!" She held the bug higher. Leo jumped again. He missed again and fell harder. Lily said, "One more time, Leo!"
Leo was tired and sore. He did not want to jump anymore. He wanted to quit. He said, "No, Lily, no more jumping. I want to rest." He ran away from the stick and hid under a rock. Lily was sad. She said, "Leo, please come back. I'm sorry. I just wanted to have fun with you."
Lily waited for Leo to come out. She saw his tail sticking out from the rock. She said, "Leo, I love you. You are a good lizard. You don't have to jump if you don't want to. Can we play something else?" She picked up a ball and rolled it to the rock. She said, "Leo, do you want to play with the ball?"
Leo peeked out from the rock. He saw the ball and Lily's smile. He felt better. He said, "Okay, Lily, I'll play with the ball. But no more sticks and bugs. They are too hard." He came out from the rock and chased the ball. Lily and Leo played with the ball. They had fun. They were friends.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a big, fierce dog named Max. He was not mean, but he looked scary. Everyone was afraid of Max because of his big teeth and loud bark.
One day, a little girl named Lily was walking to the bakery. She wanted to get a pastry for her mommy. She saw Max coming down the street. Lily was scared, but she did not run away. She stood still and looked at Max.
Max stopped and sniffed the air. He smelled the pastry in Lily's hand. He came closer to Lily, wagging his tail. Lily held out the pastry, and Max gently took it from her hand. He ate the pastry and licked his lips. From that day on, Lily and Max were best friends, and everyone in the town knew that Max was not so fierce after all.

Once upon a time, there was a hero named Tim. Tim was enthusiastic and strong. He liked to help people and animals. One day, Tim saw a little bird that could not fly. The bird was sad and needed help. Tim wanted to help the bird, so he had an idea.
Tim thought he could raise the bird up high. He found a big stick and tied the bird to the stick. Tim raised the stick up high so the bird could feel like it was flying. The bird was happy and thanked Tim for his help. But then, something unexpected happened.
As Tim raised the stick higher, the bird started to flap its wings. Suddenly, the bird could fly! The bird was not sad anymore. Tim was very happy that he could help the bird. The bird thanked Tim again and flew away. Tim was proud to be a hero and continued to help others.

Once upon a time, there was a busy nurse named Anna. She worked in a big hospital. One day, a little boy named Tim came to the hospital with his mom. Tim was sad because he had a hurt leg.
Anna the nurse saw Tim and said, "Hi, Tim! I will make your leg feel better." Tim looked at Anna and asked, "Will it hurt?" Anna smiled and said, "No, it will not hurt. I promise."
Anna put a band-aid on Tim's leg. Tim felt better and started to clap his hands. He said, "Thank you, Anna!" They both smiled and Tim went home with his mom, happy and with his leg all better.

Once there was a True car. It was blue and it made True's dad happy. He would drive it every day to work.
One day, True wanted to drive the car. His dad said, "No, you are too young to drive it, True ". But True was insistent. He said, "I can do it."
His dad reluctantly said, "Okay, but drive carefully."
So True drove the car, but he didn't keep it slow. He drove it fast and the car went bumping over the bumps. Then it started rattling and making funny noises.
True didn't know what to do, so he kept on driving. Then suddenly, the car's engine stopped working. It was so ugly. True knew he had done something wrong.
His dad was very angry. He said to True, "You should never have driven the car. Now it's broken."
True was very sad. He learnt a valuable lesson: you can't drive a car if you're too young.

Once upon a time, there was a fat cat named Kitty. She lived in a small house with a nice family. Kitty liked to play with her ball and eat her food.
One day, Kitty found a leak in the house. Water was coming out of a hole near the door. Kitty was worried and wanted to help her family. She tried to cover the hole with her body, but the water was still coming out.
Kitty's family saw what she was trying to do. They fixed the leak and stopped the water. They were so happy and thankful for Kitty's help. They gave her a big kiss and a yummy treat. Kitty felt loved and proud of herself.

Once there was a little girl who wanted to succeed. Every day she tried to do the things that were hard for her. One day, she was feeling very weak, so she curled up with her pillow and took a nap.
The next morning, she woke up feeling much better. Her pillow was as comfy as ever, and she was ready to succeed! She started off by doing some simple tasks like brushing her teeth and eating breakfast. She did those tasks very easily.
Next, she tried something more difficult. She worked very hard at it, but felt like she was not succeeding. She felt so weak she had to take another nap.
When she woke up, she felt much better. With newfound energy, she tried the task again, and this time she was able to succeed! She was very proud of herself and decided to reward herself with her pillow and a good night's sleep.

Once upon a time there was a boy named Billy. He wanted to move. He grabbed his heavy wallet and opened the door. Outside, the sun was shining brightly.
A bird flew down from a tree and perched on Billy’s shoulder.
“Where are you moving to?” the bird asked in a sweet voice.
“I’m going to a new house,” said Billy. “I can’t wait to explore!”
The bird flew off and Billy kept walking. Suddenly, he felt something heavy in his pocket. It was his wallet! He had forgotten it.
Billy stopped and smiled. He had found his wallet and could keep moving. He opened the wallet and continued walking, filled with excitement. Finally, he reached the new house and his journey had come to an end.

Once upon a time, a kind rabbit lived in a big forest. The rabbit had many friends. They would play and laugh all day long. One day, the rabbit heard a loud noise. It was a big, mean wolf. The wolf wanted to eat the rabbit.
The kind rabbit was very smart. He told the wolf, "I know a place where there is a lot of good food. I will show you if you do not eat me." The wolf thought about it and said, "Okay, show me the place."
The rabbit took the wolf to a big tree. The tree had a lot of sweet fruits. The wolf was very happy and started to eat the fruits. The rabbit told the wolf, "You can eat all the fruits you want, but do not eat the red fruit." The wolf did not listen and ate the red fruit.
Suddenly, the wolf started to laugh and could not stop. The kind rabbit had tricked the wolf. The red fruit made the wolf laugh all day and all night. The rabbit and his friends were safe, and they all laughed together. The wolf learned to be kind and became friends with the rabbit too.

Once upon a time, there was a dependable lawyer named Bob. Bob was a good friend to everyone in the town. He helped people when they needed it. Everyone liked Bob.
One day, a little girl named Sue came to Bob. She said, "Bob, I need help. My cat is stuck in a tree." Bob decided to help Sue. They went to the tree and saw the cat. The cat was very high up.
Bob and Sue tried to think of a way to get the cat down. They tried to call the cat, but it did not come down. Then, they decided to get a big stick. They used the stick to reach the cat. The cat grabbed the stick and came down. Sue was very happy and said, "Thank you, Bob!"

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a big, round ball with the number zero on it. He loved to play with his ball every day. One day, Tim lost his ball in the tall grass. He felt terrible and very sad.
Tim's mom saw him crying and asked, "What's wrong, Tim?" Tim told his mom about his lost ball with the zero on it. His mom said, "Don't worry, Tim. We will find your ball."
So, they both looked for the ball in the tall grass. Suddenly, Tim's mom found the ball and gave it to Tim. He was so happy to receive his ball back. Tim hugged his mom and said, "Thank you, Mom!" From that day on, Tim was very careful with his ball and had lots of fun playing with it. And he never felt terrible again.

One day, a group of small animals were playing in the forest. They were very happy. They were running and jumping and laughing. But then, they saw a big, confused bird. The bird was lost and did not know how to get home.
The small animals wanted to help the confused bird. They said, "Don't worry, big bird! We will save you and help you find your home!" The bird was happy and thanked the small animals.
As they all walked together, they saw a big tree. The small animals thought the tree looked strange. They went closer and saw that the tree was really a big, friendly giant! The giant said, "I know where the bird's home is! I can help you!" The small animals and the confused bird were very surprised. They all went with the giant and found the bird's home. Everyone was happy and they all became friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to build with his toy blocks. One day, Tim saw a big luggage in his room. He decided to open it.
Inside the luggage, Tim found many colorful blocks. He was very excited. Tim's friend, Sam, came over to play. They decided to have a fun game. They wanted to see who could build the tallest tower with the blocks.
Tim and Sam started to build their towers. They were having a good time. They tried to build their towers higher and higher. Tim and Sam were both very competitive. They wanted to win the game.
In the end, Tim's tower was taller than Sam's tower. Tim was very happy. But Sam was happy too, because they both had fun playing together. They put the blocks back in the luggage and decided to play again another day.

Once upon a time, a little girl named Lily went for a walk. She saw a small, cute kitten near a big tree. The kitten was sad and hungry. Lily wanted to help the kitten, so she went to find some yummy food for it.
Lily found a yummy apple and gave it to the kitten. The kitten looked at the apple and said, "I can't eat this. I need something else." Lily felt sad and started to wonder what the kitten could eat.
Then, a big bird came and dropped a yummy fish in front of the kitten. The kitten was very happy and ate the fish. Lily was happy too. She said to the bird, "Thank you for helping the kitten!" The bird smiled and said, "You're welcome. I was once a kitten too, but a magic fairy changed me into a bird. Now, I help other kittens find food." Lily and the kitten were both surprised and happy. They all became good friends and played together every day.

Once upon a time, there was a big peach tree. In the tree, there was a little bird. The little bird wanted to teach his friend, a tiny worm, how to fly. The worm thought it was a stupid idea, but he wanted to try.
The bird and the worm went to the top of the tree. The bird said, "Watch me and do what I do." The bird jumped and started to fly. The worm jumped too, but he could not fly. He fell down, down, down.
The worm landed on the ground. He was hurt and sad. The bird felt bad for the worm. They both knew it was a stupid idea. The worm could not play anymore. The bird and the worm were not happy.

Once upon a time, there was a little fan. The fan loved to stand and spin. It was very good at it. The fan had many friends who liked to watch it spin. They clapped and laughed when it spun fast.
One day, the fan felt worried. It saw a big storm coming. The storm was very loud and scary. The fan did not want its friends to get wet or hurt. It thought of a plan to help everyone.
The fan stood tall and spun as fast as it could. It blew the storm away from its friends. They were safe and dry. The fan was very happy. Its friends clapped and laughed. They thanked the fan for being so brave.

Once upon a time, there was a big red switch on a wall. No one knew what it did, but everyone was scared to touch it. A little girl named Mia was very independent and wanted to find out what the switch did.
One day, Mia decided to be brave and touch the switch. She walked up to the wall and flipped the switch. Suddenly, her toy car started to grow bigger and bigger! The car increased in size until it was as big as a real car.
Mia was so happy and excited. She had found out what the switch did, and now she had a big car to play with. She climbed into the car and drove it around, showing all her friends. They all had a great time playing with the big car, and they were not scared of the switch anymore.

One day, a pilot was flying his big plane. He saw a poor bird fall from the sky. The pilot felt sad and wanted to help the bird. He landed the plane and got out to find the bird.
The bird was on the ground and it started to cry. The pilot said, "Don't cry, little bird. I will help you." The bird stopped crying and looked at the pilot. The pilot picked up the bird and held it in his hands.
Then, something unexpected happened. The bird started to talk! The bird said, "Thank you, pilot. I was just pretending to be hurt so you would help me. I am a magic bird and now I will give you a wish!" The pilot was very surprised but happy. He wished for more friends, and the magic bird became his best friend.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Max. Max had a soft, velvet toy he loved to play with. Every day, Max would show his toy to his friends in the park.
One day, as Max was showing his velvet toy to his friends, a big wind came. The wind took Max's toy and carried it far away. Max was very sad and didn't know what to do.
Then, something unexpected happened. A bird saw the toy in the sky and caught it with its beak. The bird flew down and gave the toy back to Max. Max was so happy and thanked the bird. From that day on, Max and the bird became best friends, and they always played together with the velvet toy.

Once upon a time, there was a charming horse named Bob. Bob lived in a big, green field with many trees. He liked to run and play with his friends every day.
One day, Bob saw a little girl named Lily. Lily wanted to ride the charming horse. She asked her mom if she could pay to ride Bob. Her mom said yes and gave Lily some coins.
Lily was so happy to ride the charming horse. She paid the coins and climbed on Bob's back. They went on a fun adventure together, running and playing in the big, green field. At the end of the day, Lily gave Bob a big hug and went home with her mom. Bob felt very loved and happy.

Once upon a time, there was a Tiger called Toby. He had a special talent for dancing, which made the other animals very excited. Every day, he would practice his dance moves on the stage in the middle of the forest.
One blazing hot day, Toby decided to practice his routine near a campfire. But as he twirled and leaped in the heat, the fire burned brighter and brighter. Soon, smoke started to fill the stage and the flames began to get close to Toby.
Suddenly, an elephant nearby shouted, "Run! It's time to leave this place, Toby!" Toby smiled at his friend's thoughtful advice and quickly ran away. By the time Toby had escaped, the flames had almost reached him.
The moral of the story is that it is important to listen to wise advice. Even though it may be difficult, it can help you to stay safe and out of danger.

Once upon a time there was a Mama and a Baby. Mama and Baby were having a nice day and went for a walk. Baby saw an oat in the snow and wanted to have it. But when Baby reached for the oat, it was icy cold.
Mama said "No Baby, don't touch it. That is too cold."
Baby said, "Please Mama, I want it."
Mama said "No Baby, maybe another time."
But Baby said he wanted it so Mama gave him the icy oat. Baby bit into the oat and it was cold and hard. He wanted a kiss from Mama to make it better.
Mama said "No Baby, that won't help." But Baby begged so Mama gave Baby a kiss.
But Baby's oat was still cold and hard. He was sad. Baby cried and it was a very bad ending.

Once upon a time, there was a little ball named Rolly. Rolly loved to roll all day long. He would roll up and down the hills, and through the grass. Rolly was a very happy ball.
One day, Rolly found a network of tunnels. The tunnels were dark and scary, but Rolly wanted to roll inside them. He rolled through the tunnels, and it was a little boring because there were no hills or grass to play on.
But then, Rolly found a big room with lots of other balls. They were all rolling and playing together. Rolly joined them and had so much fun. He was happy he found the network of tunnels, even if it was a little boring at first.

One day, a little boy named Tim went for a walk. He saw an open field with lots of snow. In the field, he found an igloo. Tim was very happy and wanted to play in the igloo.
Tim tried to get inside the igloo, but he had to struggle. He was too big for the small door. Tim pushed and pushed, but he could not get in. He was sad and sat down in the snow.
Then, a little girl named Sue came to help Tim. Sue was smaller and could fit in the igloo. She went inside and made the door bigger. Now, Tim could go in too. They both played in the igloo and had a fun day.

Once upon a time, there was a little star in the sky. This star was very restless. It did not like to stay in one place. It liked to move around and play all day and night.
One day, the little star saw a big tree. The tree could bow its branches. The little star wanted to be friends with the tree. So, it came down from the sky to play with the tree. They played together and had lots of fun. The little star was very happy.
But then, something unexpected happened. The little star could not go back to the sky. It was sad and missed its home. The big tree saw the sad star and helped it. The tree bowed its branches and threw the little star back into the sky. The little star was happy to be home again. It learned that it is important to be careful when trying new things.

Once upon a time, there was a team of three friends: a cat, a dog, and a bird. They liked to play games together. One day, they found a big, weird box in the park. They were very curious about what was inside the box.
The cat said, "Let's open it!" The dog and bird agreed. But they found out that the box was locked. They tried to push and pull, but the box would not open.
Then, a little girl came to the park. She saw the team and the weird box. The girl said, "I have a key!" She used the key to unlock the box. Inside, they found lots of fun toys. The team and the little girl played together all day long. They were very happy and became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a friendly dog named Spot. Spot loved to eat sandwiches. One day, Spot saw a big sandwich on a table. He wanted to eat it. He tried to jump up, but he could not reach it.
Then, a little girl named Amy came to help. Amy had a long rope. She said, "I will tie the rope to the sandwich, and you can pull it down." Spot wagged his tail and barked happily. Amy tied the rope to the sandwich, and Spot pulled it down.
Spot and Amy were very happy to share the sandwich. They ate it together and had fun. But the sandwich was not theirs! It was for a picnic. The family who made the sandwich was sad. Spot and Amy felt bad. They learned that they should not take things that do not belong to them. From that day on, they always asked before taking something. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a smart cat named Tom. Tom lived in a house with many furniture. His favorite furniture was a big seat. Every day, Tom would sit on the seat and look out the window.
One day, Tom saw a little bird outside. He wanted to play with the bird, but the bird was scared. Tom thought, "How can I make the bird like me?" So, he decided to share his seat with the bird.
Tom opened the window and the bird flew in. They sat on the seat together and played. They became very good friends. Soon, other animals heard about Tom and the bird. They all wanted to be friends too. So, Tom shared his seat with all of them.
The animals learned that sharing is good. They all became friends and lived happily together. The moral of the story is to always share and be kind to others.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl named Lucy. She was three years old and loved playing outside. One day, Lucy was walking around her backyard, when she saw something very strange. It was a big, zero!
Lucy was so excited that she wanted to show it to her mom. She started to yell, "Mommy! Mommy! Come see the zero!"
So her mom came outside and saw the zero. She smiled and said, "That's very special, Lucy. Let's put it in the safe place".
So the mom and Lucy found a safe place to keep the zero and they put it there.
The End

One day, a little girl named Sue went to play outside. She saw a black cat sitting by a big tree. Sue wanted to be friends with the cat, so she started to skip towards it. The cat looked at her and began to skip too. They were both happy and having fun.
Sue said to the cat, "I like to skip with you. You are my friend." The cat meowed and skipped around Sue. They played together for a long time. They were very happy.
But then, a dog named Max saw them playing. Max felt jealous because he wanted to play with Sue too. He ran up to them and barked, "Can I play too?" Sue smiled and said, "Yes, Max! Let's all play together!" So Sue, the black cat, and Max the dog all skipped and played together. They became the best of friends and had lots of fun.

Once upon a time, a boy and his dad went for a walk. It was a sunny day and they wanted to explore. As they walked, they saw a hill.
"Let's go up there!" said the boy.
"Okay," said Dad.
So they started walking up the hill. It was open with lots of long grass, and the sun was shining brightly on them.
When they reached the top, they could see all the way to the horizon. It was so open! They looked all around, until the boy spotted something that made him smile.
"What is it?" asked Dad.
"A rabbit!" said the boy. He was teasing it by tickling its neck with a flower.
The rabbit didn't seem to mind. It hopped away and the boy laughed.
Dad and the boy looked around some more, enjoying the view from the top of the hill.
It was a perfect day!

Once upon a time, there was a strong boy named Tom. Tom liked to match his toys. He had a red car and a red ball. He had a blue boat and a blue hat. He also had a watch that his dad gave him. Tom loved his watch so much.
One day, Tom went to play with his friends. He wore his watch and his blue hat. They played with their cars and boats. Tom showed his friends his watch. They all liked it too.
Tom wanted to match his watch with a new toy. He saw a big tree with a pretty bird on it. The bird had many colors like his watch. Tom wanted the bird to be his friend. He climbed the tree to catch the bird. But the tree was too tall and Tom fell down. His watch broke and he was very sad.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the farm with his mom. They saw many animals and plants. Tim saw a big field with tall plants. His mom said, "That is corn, Tim. It is important food for us and the animals."
Tim wanted to show his friends the corn. He had an idea. "Mom, can we print a picture of the corn?" he asked. Mom said, "Yes, Tim, that is a great idea!"
They went home and printed a big picture of the corn. Tim showed it to his friends. They all loved it. They learned that corn was important and they wanted to visit the farm too.

Once upon a time there were two friends, Joe and Kate. Joe was always very careful and was never careless. Kate was a bit different, she liked to do things without thinking and was often careless.
One day, they decided to go to the park together to have some fun. As they were walking, Joe told Kate a funny story and they both started to laugh.
As they got to the park, Kate heard some music and she asked Joe, "What is that noise?" Joe smiled and said, "It's a dance". Kate liked the sound of dancing so she asked if Joe would dance with her.
Joe said, "Yes! I would love to dance with you". So they started to dance around the park, being careful and not careless.
They danced so much that they ended up in front of Joe's house. Joe thanked Kate for coming, and said goodbye. As he went inside his house, Joe said, "See you soon, Kate!"  and Kate said, "See you soon, Joe!"

One day, a boy was walking in the park when he saw a big, furry dog. He wanted to pet the dog, but he was too scared. He poked the dog with his finger instead. The dog was startled, but he did not seem angry. The boy hesitated, but then he decided to pet the dog.
The dog was very soft, and he liked being petted. The boy smiled. Suddenly, the sky got dark and it began to rain. The boy and the dog had to run for shelter! It was difficult to find a place where they could stay dry.
The boy used his sweater to keep the dog warm. The dog was very happy, and he licked the boy's face to thank him for his kindness. The boy laughed and patted the dog. They stayed together until the rain stopped.
The boy said goodbye to the dog and went home. He had a hard time saying goodbye, but he knew he would see the dog in the park again. With a smile on his face, the boy went home.

Once upon a time, there was an elderly man named Tom. He lived in a small, old house near the sea. Tom liked to complete puzzles and play with his dog, Spot.
One day, a big hurricane came to their town. The wind blew and the rain fell hard. Tom and Spot were scared. They hid under the table, holding each other tight. But then, something unexpected happened.
The hurricane stopped and the sun came out. Tom and Spot went outside and saw a big, beautiful rainbow in the sky. They were happy and surprised. The hurricane had left a big gift for them: a giant box of puzzles under the rainbow. Tom and Spot smiled and began to complete the puzzles together, under the bright and colorful sky.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim knew that every morning, the sun would rise. He liked to watch the sunrise because it made the sky look pretty.
One day, Tim woke up and saw that the sky was dark. He was sad because he thought he missed the sunrise. Tim's mom told him, "Don't worry, it's just a bad day. The sun will rise again tomorrow."
The next day, Tim woke up early and saw the beautiful sunrise. He was happy because he knew that even on bad days, the sun would always rise again.

Once upon a time, there was a sleepy cat named Tom. Tom loved to rub his soft fur on his family's legs. They would laugh and give Tom a big hug. Tom felt happy when he made his family smile.
One sunny day, Tom went outside to play. He saw a shiny coin on the ground. Tom did not know what it was, but he thought it had value. So, he picked it up with his mouth and took it home to show his family.
When Tom's family saw the shiny coin, they were very happy. They told Tom that it had a lot of value. They gave Tom a big hug and a special treat. Tom felt proud and loved. From that day on, Tom knew that he was a very special and sleepy cat.

One day, a little girl named Lucy went to the park with her mom. They saw a pigeon. The pigeon was walking in a funny way. Lucy thought the pigeon looked careless.
Lucy said to her mom, "Look at the pigeon, Mom! It is so funny!" Her mom smiled and said, "Yes, it is a funny pigeon. It is walking like it is dancing."
Lucy waved to the pigeon. The pigeon looked at her and waved back with its wing. Lucy laughed and clapped her hands. The pigeon walked closer to Lucy.
Lucy and the pigeon played together in the park. They danced and waved to each other. Lucy's mom watched them and smiled. They all had a fun day at the park.

Once upon a time, there was a turkey named Tim. Tim loved to play and run with his friends. One day, he saw a big bird soar high in the sky. Tim wanted to soar too.
Tim tried to soar, but he could not. His friends laughed at him. Tim felt sad and walked away. He found an empty place to be alone. Tim sat there and thought about how he could soar like the big bird.
One day, a kind wind saw Tim and wanted to help him. The wind blew strong, lifting Tim into the sky. Tim was surprised and scared, but soon he was soaring! His friends saw him and cheered. Tim was happy, and from that day on, he could soar with the help of the kind wind.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved to play with his toy board. He would draw on it, and it made him very happy. The board was big and harmless, so his mom and dad let him play with it all the time.
One day, Tim found a long string. He thought it would be fun to tie the string to his board. He tied the string tight and strong. Now, he could pull the board around the room like a train.
Tim showed his mom and dad his new toy train. They smiled and clapped their hands. They were proud of Tim for being so creative. Tim played with his board and string all day, having lots of fun. And they all lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a shy little cat named Kitty. Kitty lived in a big house with her family. One day, Kitty saw a pretty lamp in the living room. The lamp was shiny and bright. Kitty wanted to play with the lamp, but she was too shy to go near it.
One day, the sun went down and the room got dark. Kitty's family went to bed, but she couldn't sleep. She wanted to see the pretty lamp again. So, Kitty started to search for the lamp in the dark room. She looked under the table, behind the chair, and even on top of the couch.
Finally, Kitty found the pretty lamp! She was so happy that she forgot to be shy. Kitty jumped up and touched the lamp with her paw. The lamp turned on and filled the room with light. Kitty danced and played with the lamp all night long. And from that day on, Kitty was not shy anymore.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim loved cookies. One day, Tim's mom made yummy cookies for him. Tim was very happy.
Tim saw his friend, Sam, outside. He wanted to share his cookies with Sam. But suddenly, Tim had to sneeze. "Achoo!" Tim sneezed very loud. All the cookies fell on the ground. Tim was sad, and Sam was angry. "Why did you sneeze?" Sam asked. "I didn't mean to," said Tim.
Tim and Sam picked up the cookies, but they were dirty. They couldn't eat them now. Tim's mom saw what happened. She made new cookies for them. Tim and Sam learned that it's okay to make mistakes, but it's important to say sorry and fix them. They were happy again and enjoyed the cookies together.

One day, a cheerful bunny named Bobo was playing in the park. He loved to spring high into the air and land on the soft grass. Bobo was very happy when he played in the park.
Bobo saw a plastic ball near a big tree. He wanted to play with it. He used his strong legs to spring over to the ball. The ball was red and shiny. Bobo liked the ball a lot.
Bobo and the plastic ball played all day. They had so much fun in the park. When the sun went down, Bobo said goodbye to the ball and went home. He knew he would come back to play again soon.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there lived a girl named Lucy. She had a big jar of jelly. Lucy loved her jelly so much. She would eat a little bit of it every day.
One day, Lucy saw a little bird outside her window. The bird was tired and needed to rest. Lucy wanted to help the bird. She was very patient and waited for the bird to come closer.
The bird saw the jelly and wanted to eat some too. Lucy shared her jelly with the bird. They both ate the jelly and felt happy. The bird rested and felt better. Lucy and the bird became best friends. They always shared jelly and had fun together.

Once upon a time, there was a little girl. Every day she would sit in her mummy's kitchen and bake sweet muffins. She liked to watch the thick batter turn into a golden brown treat.
One day, mummy decided to surprise the little girl and brought out a fancy gold watch. She said, "Here sweetie, this watch is for you!"
The little girl was delighted. She wore the watch on her wrist and it glittered in the sun. But then, tragedy struck. As the little girl went to bake her muffins, she was so excited about her watch that she forgot to put on her thick oven mitts.
Retrieving the golden muffins from the oven, she burned her hand badly. The little girl was so scared and sad that she cried and cried.
The little girl now knows to always wear her oven mitts when baking, and she cherishes her watch even more.

Once upon a time, in a small town, there was a delicate butterfly. The butterfly liked to fly around and play with its friends. One day, the butterfly met a wise old owl. The owl told the butterfly about a special law in the town.
The law said that everyone must attach something nice to their homes. The butterfly thought this was a good idea. It wanted to make its home pretty too. So, it asked the owl, "How can I attach something nice to my home?"
The owl told the butterfly to find a beautiful flower and attach it to its home. The butterfly flew around and found the most colorful flower. It carefully attached the flower to its home. The butterfly's home looked very pretty with the flower. All its friends loved it and they all lived happily together.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a toy with a zip. He loved to play with it all day. But Tim was selfish. He did not like to share his toy with his friends.
One day, Tim's mom saw him playing alone. She wanted to encourage Tim to share. So, she told him a story about a kind boy who shared his toys and made many friends.
Tim thought about the story. He decided to share his toy with a zip. His friends were happy, and they played together. Tim was not selfish anymore. He learned that sharing can make everyone happy.

Anna loved to visit the zoo with her mom. She liked to see the big animals, like the lions and the elephants, and the small animals, like the monkeys and the penguins. She also liked to play with the toys in the gift shop, especially the stuffed animals that looked like the zoo animals.
One day, Anna saw a new toy in the gift shop. It was a stuffed giraffe with a long neck and yellow spots. Anna wanted to have it, so she asked her mom to buy it for her. Her mom said yes, and Anna hugged the giraffe happily. She named it Spot, and took it with her to see the real giraffes.
Anna was very careful with Spot, and held him close to her chest. She showed him the giraffes, and told him they were his friends. She also showed him the other animals, and told him their names. Spot seemed to like the zoo, and Anna was glad.
But then, something bad happened. Anna tripped over a rock, and fell to the ground. She was not hurt, but Spot flew out of her arms, and landed on a fence. The fence was sharp, and it tore a hole in Spot's neck. Anna saw the hole, and felt very sad. She picked up Spot, and saw his stuffing coming out. She cried, and ran to her mom.
Her mom saw Anna crying, and asked her what was wrong. Anna showed her Spot, and told her what happened. Her mom hugged her, and said she was sorry. She said they could go to the repair shop, and fix Spot. She said they could make him as good as new.
Anna nodded, and wiped her tears. She hoped the repair shop could help Spot. She wanted him to be happy, and have his original neck. She loved him very much, and did not want to lose him. She held him tight, and followed her mom to the repair shop. She hoped they would make it in time.

Once upon a time there was a little girl named Sally who lived in a big, beautiful house. One day when exploring her house, Sally discovered a mysterious chamber. She hadn't seen it before and wanted to see what was inside. She opened the door and stepped inside.
Inside the chamber, Sally faced a big problem. She saw that the room was spinning in reverse and she couldn't get out. Sally was scared and didn't know what to do. Suddenly there was a voice.
"Little one, don't be scared," the voice said. "I'm here to help you. My name is Compassionate Jasper and I'm here to help you get out."
"Thank you," replied Sally.
Compassionate Jasper was an old wizard who had the ability to reverse the spinning of the chamber. He used his magic and soon the chamber was spinning in the right direction.
"Thank you so much," said Sally. Compassionate Jasper smiled at her and said: "You are most welcome my dear. All it takes is a little compassion to get through tough problems. Goodbye!"
Sally thanked Compassionate Jasper again and stepped out of the chamber. Little did she know there were more surprises ahead!

Once upon a time, there was an elderly fisherman named Tom. Every day, Tom would go to the big blue sea to catch fish. He would remain near the shore where the water was not too deep.
One sunny day, while Tom was fishing, he saw a big fish. He said, "Wow, I want to catch that big fish!" But the big fish swam away very fast. Tom felt sad but he did not give up.
The next day, Tom went to the sea again. He saw the big fish and tried to catch it. This time, the big fish talked! It said, "Please don't catch me, Tom. I am a magic fish. If you let me go, I will give you a wish." Tom was so surprised! He let the big fish go and made a wish. Tom's wish came true, and he was happy. From that day on, Tom and the magic fish became good friends.

Once upon a time, there was a brave little dog named Copper. He loved to learn new things. Copper had many friends who liked to play with him.
One day, Copper and his friends went to the park. They played catch and had a lot of fun. Copper was very happy. The sun was shining, and the birds were singing.
Copper saw a big tree and wanted to learn how to climb it. He tried and tried, but it was hard. His friends cheered him on. Finally, Copper made it to the top of the tree. He felt very brave and proud. His friends clapped and laughed. Copper knew that learning new things was fun and exciting.

One day, a little girl named Lily went to the garden. She saw a wet onion in the dirt. Lily gazed at the onion and picked it up. She wanted to show her mom the big wet onion she found.
Lily went inside and showed her mom the onion. Her mom smiled and said, "Let's cut the onion and see what's inside." They went to the kitchen and cut the onion. Inside the onion, they found a shiny key!
Lily and her mom were very surprised. They looked all around the house to find what the key opened. Finally, they found a little box in the attic. Lily used the key to open the box. Inside, they found a pretty necklace that belonged to her grandma. Lily and her mom were so happy to find the special necklace from the wet onion.

Once upon a time, there was a little cat named Lucy. Lucy loved to lean on the big tree in her yard. One day, she saw an interesting bird on a branch. She wanted to play with the bird, so she climbed the tree.
As Lucy got closer, she saw the bird had a shiny knife in its beak. She was surprised and curious. She asked the bird, "Why do you have a knife?" The bird said, "I found it and want to give it to someone who needs it."
Lucy thought about it and said, "My friend, the dog, needs a knife to open his food." So, the bird gave the knife to Lucy. She took it to her friend, the dog. The dog was very happy and thanked Lucy and the bird.
But the dog didn't know how to use the knife. So, Lucy and the bird helped him learn. They all became good friends and played together every day. And they learned that sometimes, the most interesting things can come from unexpected places.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim who loved to run fast. One day, he saw a big tree in the park. Tim wanted to climb the tree like his parent.
Tim's parent said, "Be careful, Tim! You need to balance on the branches." Tim listened and tried to balance on the small branches. He went up and up until he was very high.
Suddenly, Tim saw a small bird in the tree. The bird was scared and couldn't fly. Tim wanted to help the bird. He moved very slowly and carefully. He reached the bird and helped it fly away. The bird was happy and so was Tim.
When Tim came down from the tree, his parent hugged him. They said, "Good job, Tim! You helped the bird by being careful and slow." Tim learned that sometimes, it's better to be slow and careful than fast. And that is the moral of the story.

Once upon a time, in a small village, there lived a mysterious cat named Tom. Tom loved to balance on things. One day, Tom found a feather in the park. He picked it up with his mouth and started to balance it on his nose.
Tom saw a little girl named Sue. Sue said, "Wow, Tom! You can balance a feather on your nose!" Tom felt proud and showed off his trick to Sue. They played together in the park all day long.
But then, something unexpected happened. A big wind came and blew the feather away. Tom and Sue were sad. They looked and looked for the feather, but they could not find it. Just when they were about to give up, a bird came down from the sky with the feather in its beak. The bird gave the feather back to Tom, and they all played together happily ever after.

Once upon a time, in a little town, there was a theater. The theater was a fun place where people went to see shows. In this town, there was also a very dependable dog named Spot. Spot was always there to help when someone needed him.
One day, a big storm came to the town. The wind blew and the rain fell hard. The people in the theater were scared. They needed help! They called for Spot, the dependable dog, to come and save them. Spot knew he had to examine the theater to make sure everyone was safe.
Spot ran to the theater and went inside. He saw that the storm had made a big mess. But Spot was brave and strong. He helped the people in the theater and made sure they were safe. The people were so happy that Spot was there to save them. They knew that Spot was a true hero. And from that day on, Spot and the people in the theater were the best of friends.

Once upon a time, there was a big orange cat named Spot. Spot loved to play with his ball. He would run and jump and catch the ball all day long.
One day, Spot's ball rolled away and got lost. Spot looked and looked for his ball, but he could not find it. He felt sad and missed his ball a lot. Spot's friend, a little bird, saw him feeling sad and wanted to help.
The little bird flew high in the sky and looked for Spot's ball. He saw it under a big tree. The bird reminded Spot to look under the tree. Spot ran to the tree and found his ball. He was so happy! Spot and the little bird played with the ball together all day long. They had so much fun and became best friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a red ball that he loved to play with. One day, he went to the park to play with his red ball. While playing, he saw a big tree with a key hanging from one of its branches. Tim was very curious about the key.
Tim asked his friend, Sally, "Do you see the key in the tree?" Sally looked up and said, "Yes, I see it! I wonder what it is for." Tim and Sally decided to watch the key to see if anything would happen. They sat under the tree and watched the key for a long time.
As they watched, a little bird flew down and picked up the key in its beak. Tim and Sally were so excited! They followed the bird to a small house. The bird used the key to open the door, and inside was a big pile of shiny, red apples. The bird shared the apples with Tim and Sally, and they all had a fun time eating the apples and playing together.

One day, a girl named Sally went to study in her room. She had a big book with fun pictures. Sally liked to look at them and learn new things. She also had a brush to paint pretty colors in her book.
One day, while Sally was studying, her brush started to move on its own. It was very unexpected! The brush was painting without Sally holding it. The brush looked sad and it painted a sad face in the book. Sally was surprised but she wanted to help the brush feel better.
Sally gave the brush a big hug and said, "Don't be sad, brush. We can paint happy things together." The brush stopped being sad and started to paint happy faces instead. Sally and the brush became best friends and they painted many happy pictures together. And from that day, they always studied and painted together, making each other happy.

One day, a clumsy dog named Spot wanted to help his mom. She was making a big salad for lunch. Spot saw a sack on the floor. He thought, "I can put the salad in the sack!"
Spot went to his mom and said, "Mom, can I help you with the salad?" His mom smiled and said, "Of course, Spot! You can put the salad in the sack." Spot felt happy and proud.
He picked up the salad with his paws, but he was clumsy. He dropped the salad on the floor! Spot felt sad. His mom said, "It's okay, Spot. We can make a new salad together." They made a new salad and put it in the sack. Spot learned that it's okay to make mistakes, and helping is always good.

One day, a little girl named Mia found a pretty bow on the ground. It was red and shiny. She picked it up and put it in her hair. Mia felt very happy.
Mia went to her friend Tom's house to show him her new bow. When she got there, she saw that Tom had a toy box. It was locked with a big lock. Tom said, "I lost the key, and now we can't play with my toys."
Mia felt sad for Tom. They looked everywhere for the key. Finally, Mia found the key under a pillow. She unlocked the toy box, and they played with the toys all day. Mia said, "I'm glad we found the key!" Tom smiled and said, "Me too, and I like your bow!"

Once upon a time, there was a big well. It was deep and wide and heavy. Each day, a little girl named Kayla played at the edge of the big well. She thought it was the most magical place in the world.
One day, Kayla had an idea. She thought it would be fun to explore the depths of the well. Without telling anyone, she grabbed a rope and tied it around her waist. She shouted down into the top of the well, expecting to hear an answer back. But all she heard was silence.
Still, Kayla was determined. She took a deep breath and jumped down. But when she reached for the rope, it was too late. The rope had become so heavy that it was impossible to pull herself back up.
Kayla was scared. She shouted and screamed, but no one came to help.
In the end, Kayla stayed stuck in the big well, never to be seen again. She had not thought about the danger of her plan.

Once upon a time, there was a little train. The train loved to push carts on the track. The train was very flexible. It could bend and turn on the track easily.
One day, the train was pushing its carts on the track. It went around a big bend. Then, something unexpected happened. The train saw a big tree on the track. The train did not know what to do.
The train thought for a moment. It used its flexible body to bend around the tree. The train pushed the carts around the tree too. The train was happy it could keep going on the track. And from that day, the train knew it could face any problem on its way.

Once upon a time, there was a graceful player named Lily. She loved to play ball with her friends. They would run, jump, and laugh together in the park.
One day, Lily saw a little boy who needed help. He was trying to reach a ball that was stuck in a tree. Lily wanted to help him, so she jumped high and got the ball down. The little boy was very happy.
From that day on, Lily and the little boy became good friends. They played ball together and helped each other whenever they could. And they lived happily ever after.

One day, a little boy named Tim went to the park with his mom. They saw a big tree with lots of red apples. Tim's mom said, "Tim, let's pick some apples!" Tim was very excited and proud to help his mom.
They picked apples together and put them in a basket. When they got home, Tim's mom said, "Let's make apple juice!" Tim was happy to help. First, they washed the apples. Then, they cut them into small pieces.
Next, they put the apple pieces into a machine. Tim's mom turned the machine on, and it made a loud noise. The machine crushed the apples and out came the juice. Tim's mom poured the juice into a glass. She gave it to Tim and said, "You did a great job helping me today!" Tim felt very proud and enjoyed his apple juice.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim had a tidy nest in a big tree. He loved his nest very much. Every day, he would make sure it was clean and nice.
One day, Tim met a new friend, a squirrel named Sam. Sam liked to listen to Tim sing. They would play and have fun together under the big tree. Tim would sing and Sam would listen with a big smile.
Soon, winter came and it was very cold. Tim and Sam helped each other stay warm. They both took turns to find food and shared it together. They were happy to have each other as friends. And when spring came, they played and listened to each other's stories in their tidy little nest under the big tree.

Once upon a time, there was a big lion who loved to roar. He lived in a high cave on a high hill. The lion had a friend, a little bird with a pretty veil on her head. They played together every day.
One day, the little bird lost her veil. She was very sad. The big lion wanted to help his friend. He roared very loud and asked all the animals to come and help find the veil.
All the animals searched high and low for the pretty veil. At last, they found it in a bush. The little bird was so happy! She thanked the big lion and all the animals for their help.
The big lion and the little bird learned that helping each other is very important. They stayed friends forever, always ready to help one another. And every time the lion roared, it was a reminder that friends should always help each other.

Nora was a compassionate three year old girl who loved to laugh and play with her little brother. One day, Nora and her brother decided to build an igloo in the backyard. They worked hard to scoop the snow and stack it into a big igloo.
Nora was very proud of their masterpiece but when she asked her mom to come take a look, her mom said, "No way!" Nora was embarrassed and thought her mom didn't like their igloo.
But then mom said, "Not tonight, I'm busy baking dinner. We can look at it tomorrow."
Nora was relieved and ran back to her brother to start building more snow sculptures. The next day, Nora and her brother showed Mom all the amazing things they had built and mom laughed and hugged them both, saying they had done a great job.
Nora was happy her mom had been so compassionate and understanding. From then on, she knew it was ok to make mistakes and that her mom would always be right there to help.

Once upon a time, there was a little raft. It was upset because it could not number how many friends it had. One day, the raft met a big fish. The fish said, "Hi, raft! I can help you number your friends."
The raft was happy. It said, "Thank you, fish!" The fish helped the raft number its friends. They counted one, two, three friends. But then, something unexpected happened.
A big wave came and pushed the raft away from its friends. The raft was upset again. But the big fish had an idea. The fish called all the raft's friends, and they worked together to bring the raft back. The raft was happy again, and it thanked the big fish and its friends for their help.

One day, a boy named Tim had a bucket. He wanted to fill it with water. He decided to go to the river near his house. He was very happy.
At the river, Tim saw a frog. The frog was sad. It wanted to go to the other side of the river. Tim decided to help the frog. He put the frog in his bucket and carried it across the river. The frog was grateful.
