But when Tim put the bucket down, the frog turned into a fairy! The fairy was happy and said, "Thank you, Tim!" She gave him a big hug. Tim was very surprised and happy. They became good friends.

Tom is a mule who lives on a farm. He likes to work hard and help the farmer. He can carry heavy things and pull the plow. He is a good mule.
One day, Tom sees a rabbit in the field. The rabbit is white and fluffy. It has long ears and a short tail. It looks very fun. Tom wants to play with the rabbit.
"Hello, rabbit," Tom says. "Can I play with you?"
The rabbit looks at Tom and smiles. "Sure, mule," it says. "Do you know how to hop?"
Tom shakes his head. He does not know how to hop. He only knows how to walk and trot and run.
The rabbit laughs. "Hop is easy," it says. "You just bend your legs and push off the ground. Like this." The rabbit hops up and down in the grass. It looks very happy.
Tom tries to hop. He bends his legs and pushes off the ground. But he is too big and heavy. He does not hop very high. He lands with a thud. He tries again and again. But he cannot hop like the rabbit.
The rabbit sees Tom trying to hop. It feels sorry for him. "Don't worry, mule," it says. "Hop is not for you. You have other things you can do. You are strong and brave and smart. You are a good mule."
Tom smiles. He is glad the rabbit is nice to him. He stops trying to hop. He walks over to the rabbit and nuzzles it with his nose. The rabbit snuggles up to him. They feel warm and cozy.
Tom and the rabbit are friends. They play together in the field. Sometimes they run and chase each other. Sometimes they sit and talk. Sometimes they just enjoy the sun and the breeze. They are happy.

Once upon a time, there was a bunny who lived in a garden. He was a very sweet bunny who loved to eat carrots. Every day, he would wake to a bright, sunny day, searching for carrots to eat.
One day, the bunny saw something different in the garden. It was a pink carrot! The bunny wanted to try it, so he hopped over and grabbed the carrot with his teeth. It was very sweet and yummy!
From then on, the bunny couldn't wait to go back to the garden every day. He searched until he found lots of pink carrots. He gained lots of energy from eating them.
One day, he hopped into his pink car and drove off into the sunshine. He had a wonderful time and gained lots of fun. He even gained a new friend along the way!

One day, a man named Bob had a wallet. He loved his wallet very much. Bob took the wallet everywhere he went. One day, he went to the store to buy food. But when he got there, he found out that his wallet was gone! Bob was very sad and did not know what to do.
Bob went back home and looked everywhere for his wallet. He looked under his bed, in the kitchen, and even in the yard. But he could not find his wallet. Then, he remembered he had a cat named Tom. Tom liked to play with things and hide them. Bob thought maybe Tom took his wallet.
Bob asked Tom, "Did you take my wallet?" Tom looked at Bob and then ran away. Bob followed Tom to a big tree in the yard. Tom climbed the tree and Bob saw his wallet up there! But there was a problem. The tree was very tall and Bob was scared to climb it. He did not know what to do.
Then, Bob had an idea. He found a long stick and used it to poke the wallet. The wallet fell from the tree and landed on the ground. But when Bob picked it up, it was dead. The wallet was shut and would not open. Bob was sad, but then he thought about Tom.
Bob looked at Tom and said, "Thank you for finding my wallet. Even though it is dead and shut, I am happy to have it back." Tom was happy too, and they both went inside to play. From that day on, Bob made sure to always keep his wallet safe and away from Tom.

Ben and Lily were playing with blocks. They liked to build towers and houses and cars. Ben had a lot of blue blocks and Lily had a lot of red blocks.
"Let's add our blocks and make a big rainbow tower!" Ben said.
"OK, that sounds fun!" Lily said. They started to add their blocks, one by one, on top of each other. They made a tall and colorful tower.
But then, Tom came along. Tom was older and bigger than Ben and Lily. He liked to make jokes, but not nice jokes. He liked to make jokes that made other kids sad or angry.
"Wow, what a silly tower!" Tom said. "It looks like a big candy cane. Can I have a bite?" He pretended to bite the tower, but he really pushed it with his hand. The tower fell down and the blocks scattered everywhere.
Ben and Lily were very sad. They had worked hard to make their tower. They did not think Tom's joke was funny. They thought it was mean.
"Tom, you are a bad boy!" Lily said. "You ruined our tower!"
"Ha ha, it was just a joke!" Tom said. "Don't be such babies. It's only blocks. You can make another one."
But Ben and Lily did not want to make another one. They were too upset. They picked up their blocks and went to find another place to play.
Tom was left alone. He looked at the mess he had made. He felt a little troubled. He wondered why Ben and Lily did not like his joke. He wondered why he had no friends to play with. He wondered if he should say sorry.

Once upon a time, there was a little bird named Tim. Tim loved to soar high in the sky. He would fly up and down and all around. All the other birds were envious of Tim because he could fly so high.
One day, Tim found a radio on the ground. He picked it up with his beak and took it to his nest. Tim liked the music that came from the radio. It made him happy, and he would dance and sing along.
Tim shared the radio with his bird friends, and they were not envious anymore. They all danced and sang together. They would take turns flying high in the sky, and then come back to dance to the music. They were all happy and had lots of fun.

Once there was an impatient skeleton. He wanted something to do, so he decided to provide a service. He started by delivering food to the hungry. Every day, he would take some food to them and put a big smile on his face.
Next, the skeleton decided to take care of the animals. He would take the cows to the meadow and give the chickens their food. He was always gentle and kind with them.
Finally, the skeleton was ready to provide a service for people. He offered to help little children cross the street safely. He made sure to always be there to guide them.
The skeleton was very happy to be able to provide so much help to others. In the end, the skeleton was no longer impatient and he was content.

Ben and Mia are friends. They like to play in the park. One day, they see a big lake. They see many boats on the lake. Some boats have sails. The sails are white and red and blue.
"Look, Ben, look!" Mia says. "The boats are so pretty. I want to go on a boat."
"Me too, Mia, me too!" Ben says. "Let's ask Mom and Dad if we can go on a boat."
They run to their parents, who are sitting on a bench. They ask them if they can go on a boat. Mom and Dad say yes. They buy tickets for a boat ride. They put on life jackets. They follow a man to a boat. The boat has a big sail. The sail is white and blue.
"Wow, this is our boat!" Mia says. "It is so big and nice."
"Yes, it is!" Ben says. "I can't wait to see the lake."
The man helps them get on the boat. He tells them to sit down and hold on. He starts the boat. The boat moves on the water. The sail catches the wind. The boat goes faster and faster. The water splashes. The wind blows. The sun shines.
Ben and Mia are happy. They laugh and clap. They see other boats. They see ducks and fish. They see trees and flowers. They see the sky. The sky is blue and high.
"Look, Mia, look!" Ben says. "The sky is so high. I can see a cloud. It looks like a bunny."
"Look, Ben, look!" Mia says. "The sky is so high. I can see a bird. It looks like a kite."
They point and clap. They have fun. They enjoy the boat ride. They thank the man. They hug Mom and Dad. They say they love the lake. They say they love the boat. They say they love the sail. They say they love the sky. They say they love each other. They are friends.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim liked to play outside. One day, it was very hot, and Tim felt tired. He saw a big tree and its shadow on the ground. Tim thought it would be a good place to sit and rest.
Tim sat down in the shadow. He saw a small, bitter fruit on the ground. Tim picked it up and looked at it. He wanted to eat it, but he remembered what his mom told him, "Do not eat things you find on the ground."
Tim put the bitter fruit back on the ground. He went back home and told his mom about it. His mom was happy that he listened to her. She gave him a sweet fruit as a treat. Tim learned that it is good to listen to his mom and not to eat things he finds outside.
The moral of the story is to always listen to your parents and be careful with what you eat.

Once upon a time there was a little girl called Molly. She was three years old and wanted to learn how to zip up her coat. One day she went to the park with her mother, who was very compassionate. As they were walking they spotted a magazine on the ground. Molly asked her mother to pick it up, which she did.
When they opened the magazine, they saw a picture of someone zipping up their coat. Molly was very excited! Her mother showed her how to do it and Molly was a quick learner. She could zip up her coat all by herself.
Molly was really proud of herself and showed off her new skill to all her friends. Everyone smiled and clapped for her. From then on, Molly learned the important skill of helping herself and also developed a compassionate heart for her friends in need.
The moral of the story is that with determination, help and support, we can all learn new things in life and be compassionate to others along the way.

One day, a little girl named Lily found a beautiful rose in the garden. She was very careful when she picked it up. Lily wanted to keep the rose, but she did not know if it belonged to someone else.
Lily asked her friends, Tom and Sue, if the rose belonged to them. Tom and Sue said no, but they wanted to find out who the rose belonged to. They all looked around the garden to find someone who was missing a rose.
Finally, they found a sad lady named Mrs. Brown. She was looking for her lost rose. Lily, Tom, and Sue gave the rose back to Mrs. Brown. She was so happy! They all learned that it is important to be careful and make sure things belong to the right person. And they all became good friends.

Once there was a little girl named Jane. Jane wanted a rock to hold. She asked her mom, but her mom said no. Jane was very impatient. She started to pout and moan.
Mom said she had to wait, but Jane was too anxious. She looked out the window and saw a big rock. It was far away.
Jane decided to go get it. She put on her shoes and ran outside. She raced to the big rock and held it tight. She was so happy she could hug it forever.
Then she heard a noise. It was her mom calling. Jane had to leave the rock and go back home. Her mom was a bit mad, but she knew that Jane just wanted something to hold.

Once upon a time, there was a puppy called Spot. Spot loved going for walks. One day Spot went for a walk to the park. Spot was excited to explore the park, so off he set.
He sniffed around until he came upon a branch. The branch was high up in a tree, so Spot couldn't reach it. He tried to climb up, but it was too slippery! Spot whimpered. What was he going to do?
Just then, Spot heard a voice. He looked up, and there was a friendly squirrel. Spot wagged his tail. The squirrel waved one of his paws, and pointed to a delicious looking nut that was nestled near the branch. Spot got an idea.
He jumped as high as he could, and managed to make the nut fall down from the branch. Spot was delighted! He took the nut and ran back to the park, where he enjoyed his special treat.

Lily and Ben were playing with their toys in the living room. Lily had a big ball that could roll and bounce. Ben had a small car that had a zipper on the back. He could open and close the zipper and put things inside the car.
"Can I play with your ball, Lily?" Ben asked.
"OK, but only for a little bit. Then you have to give it back," Lily said.
Ben took the ball and rolled it on the floor. He liked how it moved and made noise. He rolled it faster and faster, until it hit the wall and bounced back. He caught it and laughed.
Lily watched Ben and felt sad. She wanted her ball back. She liked her ball more than anything. She decided to take Ben's car while he was busy with the ball. She grabbed the car and opened the zipper. She saw a small teddy bear inside.
"Hey, that's mine!" Ben shouted. He dropped the ball and ran to Lily. He tried to take the car from her, but she held it tight.
"No, it's mine now! You have my ball!" Lily said.
They both pulled and tugged on the car, until the zipper broke. The teddy bear fell out and landed on the floor. They both stopped and looked at the broken car and the teddy bear.
They felt sad and sorry. They had ruined their toys and their fun. They looked at each other and said, "I'm sorry."
They hugged and said, "I'm sorry, too."
They picked up their toys and decided to share. They rolled the ball and drove the car together. They put the teddy bear inside the car and closed the zipper. They smiled and played happily.

One day, a gentle cat named Lily went for a walk. She found a big box of chalk on the ground. Lily thought, "I can draw with this!"
Lily picked up the chalk and started to draw a big sun. A little boy named Tim saw her and said, "Wow, a cat can draw!" They both laughed together.
Then, something unexpected happened. The sun that Lily drew came to life and started to dance! Lily and Tim were so happy and laughed even more. They played with the dancing sun all day long.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim was enthusiastic about being a hero. He had a toy sword that he loved to play with. He would run around the house with it, pretending to save the day.
One day, Tim saw a cat stuck in a tree. He wanted to help the cat. So, Tim grabbed his sword and went to the tree. He looked up and said, "Don't worry, cat, I will save you!"
Tim tried to use his sword to reach the cat. But the sword was not long enough. He thought very hard and had an idea. Tim found a big stick and used his sword to push the stick up to the cat. The cat jumped onto the stick and came down safely.
"Thank you, Tim!" said the cat. "You are a real hero!" Tim felt very happy and proud. He knew that being a hero was not just about having a sword, but also about helping others.

Once there was a little boy named Tim. He had a big watch. The watch was very pretty. Tim loved to wear his watch.
One day, Tim met a nice girl named Sue. She saw his watch and asked a question. "Can I see your watch?" Sue said. Tim was polite and showed Sue his watch. They looked at the watch together.
They became good friends. Tim and Sue played and talked every day. They learned to share and be polite. And they always remembered the day they met because of the watch.

Once upon a time, there was a big cat and a small mouse. They lived in a house. The cat wanted to catch the mouse, but the mouse was very alert. The mouse knew that the cat had the power to catch him, so he was always careful.
One day, the cat saw the mouse near his food. The cat jumped to catch him, but the mouse was too fast. The cat tried again and again, but the mouse always got away. The cat was not happy, and the mouse knew he could not yield to the cat.
The cat thought of a plan. He would pretend to be asleep, and when the mouse came close, he would catch him. But the mouse was too smart for the cat. The mouse saw the cat pretending to sleep and did not go near him. The cat tried many times, but the mouse never came close.
In the end, the cat learned that he could not catch the smart mouse. The cat and the mouse became friends and shared the food in the house. They learned that it was better to be friends than to fight. The cat and the mouse were happy, and they lived together in the house.

Once, there was a boy named Jack. Every day, Jack liked to make things. He made boats out of paper, dollhouses out of boxes and even a castle out of old blocks.
One day, Jack wanted to make something special. He found a big bucket and filled it with water. Then he grabbed some special paints and decorated the bucket. He painted it all sorts of beautiful colours, including a big red heart.
When the bucket was done, Jack tested it out to see if it would hold water. But when he put water inside it, the bucket started to leak!
Jack got worried. But then he had an idea. He ran to the garden, grabbed some mud and sealed the hole where the water was leaking. His bucket was now as good as new.
The bucket looked so beautiful that Jack decided to use it as a special planter. He added soil and planted some colorful flowers and now it looks like a beautiful garden.
Jack was very proud of the bucket he had made. Every time he skipped by, the bucket made him smile.

Once upon a time, in a big forest, there was a small stream. A little bird named Lily lived near the stream. Lily was very foolish. She did not know how to set her nest. She tried to set it on the ground, but it was not safe there.
One day, a big wind came and blew Lily's nest away. She was sad and did not know what to do. Then, she saw a big fish in the stream. The fish saw Lily was sad and asked, "Why are you sad?" Lily told the fish about her nest.
The big fish had an idea. He told Lily to set her nest on a tree near the stream. Lily thought it was a good idea. She set her nest on the tree and was very happy. But then, something unexpected happened.
The big fish jumped out of the stream and tried to eat Lily's eggs! Lily was scared, but she was brave too. She pushed the big fish back into the stream. The big fish was sad because he could not eat the eggs.
In the end, Lily learned not to trust everyone. She knew that she should be careful when setting her nest. She set her nest in a safer place and lived happily with her eggs.

Once upon a time, in a small house, there was a gray cat named Luna. Luna loved to play with yarn. One day, Luna saw a big ball of yarn on the table. She wanted to carry it to her bed to play with it.
Luna jumped up and tried to carry the yarn in her mouth. But the yarn was too big! She tried and tried, but it was hard. Luna's friend, a little girl named Emma, saw Luna trying to carry the yarn. Emma said, "Luna, do you need help?"
"Yes, please," meowed Luna. Emma helped Luna carry the big ball of yarn to her bed. They played together all day with the yarn, rolling it and chasing it. Luna was very happy that her friend Emma helped her. And they lived happily ever after.

Once upon a time, there was a little boy named Tim. Tim had a brother named Sam. They loved to play together. They played with their toys and ran around in the park. It was easy for them to have fun.
One day, Tim and Sam found a big piece of paper. They decided to make a big picture. Tim drew a house and Sam drew a tree. They were very happy with their picture. But then, Tim accidentally made a tear in the paper.
Tim was sad and Sam was sad too. They didn't want their picture to have a tear. So, they thought of a plan. They found some tape and put it on the tear. Now, the picture was fixed and they were happy again.
Tim and Sam showed their picture to their mom and dad. Mom and dad were proud of them. They hung the picture on the wall. Tim and Sam were happy that they could fix the tear and save their picture. They knew that working together made things easy.
